claim: A Claude Code PreToolUse command hook receives JSON on stdin with the tool name and, for Bash, the command text at tool_input.command plus the working directory in cwd. It blocks a call either by exiting with code 2 and writing the reason to stderr, or by exiting 0 and printing JSON whose hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision is deny. Exiting 0 with no output gives no opinion and never approves. Hooks are configured under a hooks key in a settings file (project .claude/settings.json is committable) as event, then matcher group, then handler. The optional if filter on a handler is best-effort, so enforcement logic should inspect the command inside the hook script rather than rely on the filter alone.
